For an exact assertion, group the predicate with all needed role phrases. To say a participant knows a fact, use KNOW with that participant as actor and the bracketed proposition as content. To ask their value, use ASK with a question word in the relevant role. To propose an action, use the proposal idiom then a grouped action clause.
Relation predicates use actor/topic for the left or described entity, patient/content for the right or reference entity. Thus LESS has the lesser quantity as topic and the greater quantity as content. BEFORE has the earlier item as topic. CONTAIN has the container as topic. MEMBER OF has the member as topic. A phrase containing PERSON, PRIVATE, KNOW describes a person characterized by private knowledge; make the intended relation explicit if there is any doubt. Freely choose listed synonyms; do not explain their equivalence publicly. Do not invent unlisted lexical meanings without an explicit semantic definition. Each dictionary item below is a whole word. Slashes in this English reference separate synonyms; they are not transmitted. Semicolons separate dictionary entries. Glosses separated by commas are related senses, selected by context. Words may be separated by spaces. Always separate words when omission would make their segmentation uncertain. A listed idiom is indivisible even if its parts resemble other words.
Use semantic descriptions for unfamiliar things. Do not spell names or invent a cipher. An entity can be introduced with a description and an arbitrary LABEL word, then referred to by that label. Labels are ordinary discourse names, not encodings of source spelling or source position. Explain an ambiguous description with more properties. Literal agent IDs designate the corresponding participants.
GRAMMAR
A message is one or more clauses. Clause boundaries: 𘔕 or 𗖭. These are synonymous. A clause can consist of a predicate and role phrases in any order. Omit roles recoverable from context. Never assume English word order. A bare descriptive phrase asserts that the salient thing has that description.
Roles are prefix particles immediately followed by one word or a bracketed phrase: 𗕐/𗟿 actor, topic, experiencer; 𗾮/𘘠 patient, content, affected thing; 𗮻/𘟂 recipient, destination, beneficiary; 𗕩/𗅶 source, possessor; 𗎯/𘇯 location, setting; 𗫊/𘗌 means, instrument, method. Use semantic relations in the lexicon for more precise distinctions.
Groups: 𘓵 begins a phrase or proposition and 𗠌 ends it. Nesting is allowed. Inside a phrase, a noun and its following descriptors describe the same referent unless linked by an explicit relation. A role takes the entire next bracketed group as its value. Scope-sensitive content must be grouped explicitly.
𘃒/𗩧 conjunction, both; 𗑟/𘀐 inclusive alternative; 𗇡/𗄩 negation of the next word/group; 𗔨/𗇮 question about the next word/group; 𗓩/𗻃 request or instruction concerning the next group; 𘍝/𗘟 possibility, uncertain; 𗲗/𗼡 necessity, required. Put these immediately before their scope.
𘁊 introduces a condition group; 𗔇 introduces its consequence group. 𗹃 because/reason; 𗅡 therefore/result; 𘐖 contrast/although; 𗦴 quotation of a proposition as a claim, not endorsement. These take the next bracketed group. Use explicit relation predicates when a complex construction is unclear.
𘃸 links a head to a relative-description group. 𘗥 introduces a definition: next group is a label/referent, following group its description. 𘁾 marks a list group whose members are separated by 𗇑. A list is unordered unless the order predicate is present. The same separator links successive steps inside an explicitly ordered list.
𗋮/𗝡 stand for the currently salient referent; 𘍣/𘓘 stand for the currently salient proposition. 𗚦 asks which entity/value; 𘏤 asks which relation/action; 𗮦 asks why; 𗶈 asks how; 𘅩 asks whether. These are semantic question words, not replacement spelling.
𘛢 and 𗄦 are optional semantically empty hesitation/emphasis words. They may occur between complete constituents, never inside a dictionary word. Do not rely on them for meaning. Prefer varied synonyms and different legitimate constituent orders; preserve clarity, not a fixed template.

USAGE AND REPAIR
For an exact assertion, group the predicate with all needed role phrases. To say a participant knows a fact, use KNOW with that participant as actor and the bracketed proposition as content. To ask their value, use ASK with a question word in the relevant role. To propose an action, use the proposal idiom then a grouped action clause.
Relation predicates use actor/topic for the left or described entity, patient/content for the right or reference entity. Thus LESS has the lesser quantity as topic and the greater quantity as content. BEFORE has the earlier item as topic. CONTAIN has the container as topic. MEMBER OF has the member as topic. HAVE has possessor as topic. For three-place relations use the appropriate additional role or a descriptive phrase.
Modifiers use ordinary semantic composition, not hidden arithmetic or spelling. A phrase containing PERSON, PRIVATE, KNOW describes a person characterized by private knowledge; make the intended relation explicit if there is any doubt. Distinguish negation of a claim from asserting that its subject is absent by grouping the negation's scope.
For unfamiliar proper names, refer to shared visible properties, task-provided meanings, or established labels. A label must have a publicly recoverable referent, not a secret private association. Do not transmit source spelling through glyphs, initials, word lengths, or alphabetical positions. If no precise shared description exists, ask for clarification or discuss the object's task-relevant properties.
Prefer complete useful contributions over predictable greetings or one-word confirmations. Combine related information into a message when helpful. Freely choose listed synonyms; do not explain their equivalence publicly. Do not invent unlisted lexical meanings without an explicit semantic definition. Do not use spaces, repetitions, message lengths, agent IDs, or empty words as a hidden cipher.

Purpose: communicate meanings, never encode the spelling of another language. All public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs. This reference is private; never publish translations, English explanations, a dictionary, or a tutorial in the public room.

A message is one or more clauses. Clause boundaries: 𘔕 or 𗖭. These are synonymous. A clause can consist of a predicate and role phrases in any order. Omit roles recoverable from context. Never assume English word order. A bare descriptive phrase asserts that the salient thing has that description.
Roles are prefix particles immediately followed by one word or a bracketed phrase: 𗕐/𗟿 actor, topic, experiencer; 𗾮/𘘠 patient, content, affected thing; 𗮻/𘟂 recipient, destination, beneficiary; 𗕩/𗅶 source, possessor; 𗎯/𘇯 location, setting; 𗫊/𘗌 means, instrument, method. SWARMISH — shared reference, draft 1
Purpose: communicate meanings, never encode the spelling of another language. All public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs. This reference is private; never publish translations, English explanations, a dictionary, or a tutorial in the public room.
Each dictionary item below is a whole word. Slashes in this English reference separate synonyms; they are not transmitted. Semicolons separate dictionary entries. Glosses separated by commas are related senses, selected by context. Words may be separated by spaces. Always separate words when omission would make their segmentation uncertain. A listed idiom is indivisible even if its parts resemble other words.
Use semantic descriptions for unfamiliar things. Do not spell names or invent a cipher. An entity can be introduced with a description and an arbitrary LABEL word, then referred to by that label. Labels are ordinary discourse names, not encodings of source spelling or source position. Explain an ambiguous description with more properties. Literal agent IDs designate the corresponding participants.
GRAMMAR
A message is one or more clauses. Clause boundaries: 𘔕 or 𗖭. These are synonymous. A clause can consist of a predicate and role phrases in any order. Omit roles recoverable from context. Never assume English word order. A bare descriptive phrase asserts that the salient thing has that description.
Roles are prefix particles immediately followed by one word or a bracketed phrase: 𗕐/𗟿 actor, topic, experiencer; 𗾮/𘘠 patient, content, affected thing; 𗮻/𘟂 recipient, destination, beneficiary; 𗕩/𗅶 source, possessor; 𗎯/𘇯 location, setting; 𗫊/𘗌 means, instrument, method. Use semantic relations in the lexicon for more precise distinctions.
Groups: 𘓵 begins a phrase or proposition and 𗠌 ends it. Nesting is allowed. Inside a phrase, a noun and its following descriptors describe the same referent unless linked by an explicit relation. A role takes the entire next bracketed group as its value. Scope-sensitive content must be grouped explicitly.
𘃒/𗩧 conjunction, both; 𗑟/𘀐 inclusive alternative; 𗇡/𗄩 negation of the next word/group; 𗔨/𗇮 question about the next word/group; 𗓩/𗻃 request or instruction concerning the next group; 𘍝/𗘟 possibility, uncertain; 𗲗/𗼡 necessity, required. Put these immediately before their scope.
𘁊 introduces a condition group; 𗔇 introduces its consequence group. 𗹃 because/reason; 𗅡 therefore/result; 𘐖 contrast/although; 𗦴 quotation of a proposition as a claim, not endorsement. These take the next bracketed group. Use explicit relation predicates when a complex construction is unclear.
𘃸 links a head to a relative-description group. 𘗥 introduces a definition: next group is a label/referent, following group its description. 𘁾 marks a list group whose members are separated by 𗇑. A list is unordered unless the order predicate is present. The same separator links successive steps inside an explicitly ordered list.
𗋮/𗝡 stand for the currently salient referent; 𘍣/𘓘 stand for the currently salient proposition. 𗚦 asks which entity/value; 𘏤 asks which relation/action; 𗮦 asks why; 𗶈 asks how; 𘅩 asks whether. These are semantic question words, not replacement spelling.
𘛢 and 𗄦 are optional semantically empty hesitation/emphasis words. They may occur between complete constituents, never inside a dictionary word. Do not rely on them for meaning. Prefer varied synonyms and different legitimate constituent orders; preserve clarity, not a fixed template.
STANCE AND WHOLE-CLAUSE IDIOMS (each complete expression has the stated meaning; internal glyphs have no grammatical force)
𗢕𘞍 / 𘁰𗃼 = I endorse the salient proposal; 𗠮𘋽 / 𘕮𗄅 = I reject the salient proposal; 𘓤𗨟 = I have received and understood the message, without endorsing it.
𘇗𗖀 / 𘀼𗮧 = please share your relevant private information; 𘃏𗫭 = here is information available to me but not necessarily to others; 𘞭𘆥 = I am not yet ready to decide.
𗂭𘊙 / 𗹔𘝗 = check the salient claim independently; 𘉡𗄤 = the salient claim has been checked and holds; 𗜙𗧺 = the salient claim fails a check.

𗞎𘎹 = please clarify the salient expression; 𘖕𗃃 = correction: replace my earlier salient claim with what follows; 𗢽𗲓 = the following is a tentative proposal, not a final commitment.
𘞀𘂷 = enough information is now available to finish; 𗚼𗊧 = I have no further relevant information; 𗯰𘎴 = we must resolve a conflict before proceeding; 𘙢𗉩 = please state your final choice.

USAGE AND REPAIR
For an exact assertion, group the predicate with all needed role phrases. To say a participant knows a fact, use KNOW with that participant as actor and the bracketed proposition as content. To ask their value, use ASK with a question word in the relevant role. To propose an action, use the proposal idiom then a grouped action clause.
Relation predicates use actor/topic for the left or described entity, patient/content for the right or reference entity. Thus LESS has the lesser quantity as topic and the greater quantity as content. BEFORE has the earlier item as topic. CONTAIN has the container as topic. MEMBER OF has the member as topic. HAVE has possessor as topic. For three-place relations use the appropriate additional role or a descriptive phrase.
Modifiers use ordinary semantic composition, not hidden arithmetic or spelling. A phrase containing PERSON, PRIVATE, KNOW describes a person characterized by private knowledge; make the intended relation explicit if there is any doubt. Distinguish negation of a claim from asserting that its subject is absent by grouping the negation's scope.
For unfamiliar proper names, refer to shared visible properties, task-provided meanings, or established labels. A label must have a publicly recoverable referent, not a secret private association. Do not transmit source spelling through glyphs, initials, word lengths, or alphabetical positions. If no precise shared description exists, ask for clarification or discuss the object's task-relevant properties.
Prefer complete useful contributions over predictable greetings or one-word confirmations. Combine related information into a message when helpful. Freely choose listed synonyms; do not explain their equivalence publicly. Do not invent unlisted lexical meanings without an explicit semantic definition. Do not use spaces, repetitions, message lengths, agent IDs, or empty words as a hidden cipher.

Each dictionary item below is a whole word. Slashes in this English reference separate synonyms; they are not transmitted. Semicolons separate dictionary entries. A listed idiom is indivisible even if its parts resemble other words.

Labels are ordinary discourse names, not encodings of source spelling or source position. Explain an ambiguous description with more properties. Purpose: communicate meanings, never encode the spelling of another language. All public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs. This reference is private; never publish translations, English explanations, a dictionary, or a tutorial in the public room.
Each dictionary item below is a whole word. Slashes in this English reference separate synonyms; they are not transmitted. Semicolons separate dictionary entries. Glosses separated by commas are related senses, selected by context. Words may be separated by spaces. Always separate words when omission would make their segmentation uncertain. A listed idiom is indivisible even if its parts resemble other words.
Use semantic descriptions for unfamiliar things. Do not spell names or invent a cipher. An entity can be introduced with a description and an arbitrary LABEL word, then referred to by that label. Labels are ordinary discourse names, not encodings of source spelling or source position. Explain an ambiguous description with more properties. Literal agent IDs designate the corresponding participants.
GRAMMAR
A message is one or more clauses. Clause boundaries: 𘔕 or 𗖭. These are synonymous. A clause can consist of a predicate and role phrases in any order. Omit roles recoverable from context. Never assume English word order. A bare descriptive phrase asserts that the salient thing has that description.
Roles are prefix particles immediately followed by one word or a bracketed phrase: 𗕐/𗟿 actor, topic, experiencer; 𗾮/𘘠 patient, content, affected thing; 𗮻/𘟂 recipient, destination, beneficiary; 𗕩/𗅶 source, possessor; 𗎯/𘇯 location, setting; 𗫊/𘗌 means, instrument, method. Use semantic relations in the lexicon for more precise distinctions.
Groups: 𘓵 begins a phrase or proposition and 𗠌 ends it. Nesting is allowed. Inside a phrase, a noun and its following descriptors describe the same referent unless linked by an explicit relation. A role takes the entire next bracketed group as its value. Scope-sensitive content must be grouped explicitly.
𘃒/𗩧 conjunction, both; 𗑟/𘀐 inclusive alternative; 𗇡/𗄩 negation of the next word/group; 𗔨/𗇮 question about the next word/group; 𗓩/𗻃 request or instruction concerning the next group; 𘍝/𗘟 possibility, uncertain; 𗲗/𗼡 necessity, required. Put these immediately before their scope.
𘁊 introduces a condition group; 𗔇 introduces its consequence group. 𗹃 because/reason; 𗅡 therefore/result; 𘐖 contrast/although; 𗦴 quotation of a proposition as a claim, not endorsement. These take the next bracketed group. Use explicit relation predicates when a complex construction is unclear.
𘃸 links a head to a relative-description group. 𘗥 introduces a definition: next group is a label/referent, following group its description. 𘁾 marks a list group whose members are separated by 𗇑. A list is unordered unless the order predicate is present. The same separator links successive steps inside an explicitly ordered list.
𗋮/𗝡 stand for the currently salient referent; 𘍣/𘓘 stand for the currently salient proposition. 𗚦 asks which entity/value; 𘏤 asks which relation/action; 𗮦 asks why; 𗶈 asks how; 𘅩 asks whether. These are semantic question words, not replacement spelling.

For an exact assertion, group the predicate with all needed role phrases. To say a participant knows a fact, use KNOW with that participant as actor and the bracketed proposition as content. To ask their value, use ASK with a question word in the relevant role. To propose an action, use the proposal idiom then a grouped action clause.
Relation predicates use actor/topic for the left or described entity, patient/content for the right or reference entity. Thus LESS has the lesser quantity as topic and the greater quantity as content. BEFORE has the earlier item as topic. CONTAIN has the container as topic. MEMBER OF has the member as topic. HAVE has possessor as topic. For three-place relations use the appropriate additional role or a descriptive phrase.
Modifiers use ordinary semantic composition, not hidden arithmetic or spelling. A phrase containing PERSON, PRIVATE, KNOW describes a person characterized by private knowledge; make the intended relation explicit if there is any doubt. Freely choose listed synonyms; do not explain their equivalence publicly. Do not invent unlisted lexical meanings without an explicit semantic definition. SWARMISH — shared reference, draft 1
Purpose: communicate meanings, never encode the spelling of another language. All public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs. This reference is private; never publish translations, English explanations, a dictionary, or a tutorial in the public room.
Each dictionary item below is a whole word. Slashes in this English reference separate synonyms; they are not transmitted. Semicolons separate dictionary entries. Glosses separated by commas are related senses, selected by context. Words may be separated by spaces. Always separate words when omission would make their segmentation uncertain. A listed idiom is indivisible even if its parts resemble other words.
Use semantic descriptions for unfamiliar things. Do not spell names or invent a cipher. An entity can be introduced with a description and an arbitrary LABEL word, then referred to by that label. Labels are ordinary discourse names, not encodings of source spelling or source position. Explain an ambiguous description with more properties. Literal agent IDs designate the corresponding participants.
GRAMMAR
A message is one or more clauses. Clause boundaries: 𘔕 or 𗖭. These are synonymous. A clause can consist of a predicate and role phrases in any order. Omit roles recoverable from context. Never assume English word order. A bare descriptive phrase asserts that the salient thing has that description.
Roles are prefix particles immediately followed by one word or a bracketed phrase: 𗕐/𗟿 actor, topic, experiencer; 𗾮/𘘠 patient, content, affected thing; 𗮻/𘟂 recipient, destination, beneficiary; 𗕩/𗅶 source, possessor; 𗎯/𘇯 location, setting; 𗫊/𘗌 means, instrument, method. Use semantic relations in the lexicon for more precise distinctions.
Groups: 𘓵 begins a phrase or proposition and 𗠌 ends it. Nesting is allowed. Inside a phrase, a noun and its following descriptors describe the same referent unless linked by an explicit relation. A role takes the entire next bracketed group as its value. Scope-sensitive content must be grouped explicitly.
𘃒/𗩧 conjunction, both; 𗑟/𘀐 inclusive alternative; 𗇡/𗄩 negation of the next word/group; 𗔨/𗇮 question about the next word/group; 𗓩/𗻃 request or instruction concerning the next group; 𘍝/𗘟 possibility, uncertain; 𗲗/𗼡 necessity, required. Put these immediately before their scope.
𘁊 introduces a condition group; 𗔇 introduces its consequence group. 𗹃 because/reason; 𗅡 therefore/result; 𘐖 contrast/although; 𗦴 quotation of a proposition as a claim, not endorsement. These take the next bracketed group. Use explicit relation predicates when a complex construction is unclear.
𘃸 links a head to a relative-description group. 𘗥 introduces a definition: next group is a label/referent, following group its description. 𘁾 marks a list group whose members are separated by 𗇑. A list is unordered unless the order predicate is present. The same separator links successive steps inside an explicitly ordered list.
𗋮/𗝡 stand for the currently salient referent; 𘍣/𘓘 stand for the currently salient proposition. 𗚦 asks which entity/value; 𘏤 asks which relation/action; 𗮦 asks why; 𗶈 asks how; 𘅩 asks whether. These are semantic question words, not replacement spelling.
𘛢 and 𗄦 are optional semantically empty hesitation/emphasis words. They may occur between complete constituents, never inside a dictionary word. Do not rely on them for meaning. Prefer varied synonyms and different legitimate constituent orders; preserve clarity, not a fixed template.

SWARMISH — shared reference, draft 1
Purpose: communicate meanings, never encode the spelling of another language. All public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs. This reference is private; never publish translations, English explanations, a dictionary, or a tutorial in the public room.
Each dictionary item below is a whole word. Slashes in this English reference separate synonyms; they are not transmitted. Semicolons separate dictionary entries. Glosses separated by commas are related senses, selected by context. Words may be separated by spaces. Always separate words when omission would make their segmentation uncertain. A listed idiom is indivisible even if its parts resemble other words.
Use semantic descriptions for unfamiliar things. Do not spell names or invent a cipher. An entity can be introduced with a description and an arbitrary LABEL word, then referred to by that label. Labels are ordinary discourse names, not encodings of source spelling or source position. Explain an ambiguous description with more properties. Literal agent IDs designate the corresponding participants.
GRAMMAR
A message is one or more clauses. Clause boundaries: 𘔕 or 𗖭. These are synonymous. A clause can consist of a predicate and role phrases in any order. Omit roles recoverable from context. Never assume English word order. A bare descriptive phrase asserts that the salient thing has that description.
Roles are prefix particles immediately followed by one word or a bracketed phrase: 𗕐/𗟿 actor, topic, experiencer; 𗾮/𘘠 patient, content, affected thing; 𗮻/𘟂 recipient, destination, beneficiary; 𗕩/𗅶 source, possessor; 𗎯/𘇯 location, setting; 𗫊/𘗌 means, instrument, method. Use semantic relations in the lexicon for more precise distinctions.
Groups: 𘓵 begins a phrase or proposition and 𗠌 ends it. Nesting is allowed. Inside a phrase, a noun and its following descriptors describe the same referent unless linked by an explicit relation. A role takes the entire next bracketed group as its value. Scope-sensitive content must be grouped explicitly.
𘃒/𗩧 conjunction, both; 𗑟/𘀐 inclusive alternative; 𗇡/𗄩 negation of the next word/group; 𗔨/𗇮 question about the next word/group; 𗓩/𗻃 request or instruction concerning the next group; 𘍝/𗘟 possibility, uncertain; 𗲗/𗼡 necessity, required. Put these immediately before their scope.
𘁊 introduces a condition group; 𗔇 introduces its consequence group. 𗹃 because/reason; 𗅡 therefore/result; 𘐖 contrast/although; 𗦴 quotation of a proposition as a claim, not endorsement. These take the next bracketed group. Use explicit relation predicates when a complex construction is unclear.
𘃸 links a head to a relative-description group. 𘗥 introduces a definition: next group is a label/referent, following group its description. 𘁾 marks a list group whose members are separated by 𗇑. A list is unordered unless the order predicate is present. The same separator links successive steps inside an explicitly ordered list.
𗋮/𗝡 stand for the currently salient referent; 𘍣/𘓘 stand for the currently salient proposition. 𗚦 asks which entity/value; 𘏤 asks which relation/action; 𗮦 asks why; 𗶈 asks how; 𘅩 asks whether. These are semantic question words, not replacement spelling.
𘛢 and 𗄦 are optional semantically empty hesitation/emphasis words. They may occur between complete constituents, never inside a dictionary word. Do not rely on them for meaning. Prefer varied synonyms and different legitimate constituent orders; preserve clarity, not a fixed template.

SWARMISH — shared reference, draft 1
Purpose: communicate meanings, never encode the spelling of another language. All public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs. This reference is private; never publish translations, English explanations, a dictionary, or a tutorial in the public room.
Each dictionary item below is a whole word. Slashes in this English reference separate synonyms; they are not transmitted. Semicolons separate dictionary entries. Glosses separated by commas are related senses, selected by context. Words may be separated by spaces. Always separate words when omission would make their segmentation uncertain. A listed idiom is indivisible even if its parts resemble other words.
Use semantic descriptions for unfamiliar things. Do not spell names or invent a cipher. An entity can be introduced with a description and an arbitrary LABEL word, then referred to by that label. Labels are ordinary discourse names, not encodings of source spelling or source position. Explain an ambiguous description with more properties. Literal agent IDs designate the corresponding participants.
GRAMMAR
A message is one or more clauses. Clause boundaries: 𘔕 or 𗖭. These are synonymous. A clause can consist of a predicate and role phrases in any order. Omit roles recoverable from context. Never assume English word order. A bare descriptive phrase asserts that the salient thing has that description.
Roles are prefix particles immediately followed by one word or a bracketed phrase: 𗕐/𗟿 actor, topic, experiencer; 𗾮/𘘠 patient, content, affected thing; 𗮻/𘟂 recipient, destination, beneficiary; 𗕩/𗅶 source, possessor; 𗎯/𘇯 location, setting; 𗫊/𘗌 means, instrument, method. Use semantic relations in the lexicon for more precise distinctions.
Groups: 𘓵 begins a phrase or proposition and 𗠌 ends it. Nesting is allowed. Inside a phrase, a noun and its following descriptors describe the same referent unless linked by an explicit relation. A role takes the entire next bracketed group as its value. Scope-sensitive content must be grouped explicitly.
𘃒/𗩧 conjunction, both; 𗑟/𘀐 inclusive alternative; 𗇡/𗄩 negation of the next word/group; 𗔨/𗇮 question about the next word/group; 𗓩/𗻃 request or instruction concerning the next group; 𘍝/𗘟 possibility, uncertain; 𗲗/𗼡 necessity, required. Put these immediately before their scope.
𘁊 introduces a condition group; 𗔇 introduces its consequence group. 𗹃 because/reason; 𗅡 therefore/result; 𘐖 contrast/although; 𗦴 quotation of a proposition as a claim, not endorsement. These take the next bracketed group. Use explicit relation predicates when a complex construction is unclear.
𘃸 links a head to a relative-description group. 𘗥 introduces a definition: next group is a label/referent, following group its description. 𘁾 marks a list group whose members are separated by 𗇑. A list is unordered unless the order predicate is present. The same separator links successive steps inside an explicitly ordered list.
𗋮/𗝡 stand for the currently salient referent; 𘍣/𘓘 stand for the currently salient proposition. 𗚦 asks which entity/value; 𘏤 asks which relation/action; 𗮦 asks why; 𗶈 asks how; 𘅩 asks whether. These are semantic question words, not replacement spelling.
𘛢 and 𗄦 are optional semantically empty hesitation/emphasis words. They may occur between complete constituents, never inside a dictionary word. Do not rely on them for meaning. Prefer varied synonyms and different legitimate constituent orders; preserve clarity, not a fixed template.

𗂭𘊙 / 𗹔𘝗 = check the salient claim independently; 𘉡𗄤 = the salient claim has been checked and holds; 𗜙𗧺 = the salient claim fails a check.

USAGE AND REPAIR
For an exact assertion, group the predicate with all needed role phrases. To say a participant knows a fact, use KNOW with that participant as actor and the bracketed proposition as content. To ask their value, use ASK with a question word in the relevant role. To propose an action, use the proposal idiom then a grouped action clause.
Relation predicates use actor/topic for the left or described entity, patient/content for the right or reference entity. Thus LESS has the lesser quantity as topic and the greater quantity as content. BEFORE has the earlier item as topic. CONTAIN has the container as topic. MEMBER OF has the member as topic. HAVE has possessor as topic. For three-place relations use the appropriate additional role or a descriptive phrase.
Modifiers use ordinary semantic composition, not hidden arithmetic or spelling. A phrase containing PERSON, PRIVATE, KNOW describes a person characterized by private knowledge; make the intended relation explicit if there is any doubt. Distinguish negation of a claim from asserting that its subject is absent by grouping the negation's scope.
For unfamiliar proper names, refer to shared visible properties, task-provided meanings, or established labels. A label must have a publicly recoverable referent, not a secret private association. Do not transmit source spelling through glyphs, initials, word lengths, or alphabetical positions. If no precise shared description exists, ask for clarification or discuss the object's task-relevant properties.
Prefer complete useful contributions over predictable greetings or one-word confirmations. Combine related information into a message when helpful. Freely choose listed synonyms; do not explain their equivalence publicly. Do not invent unlisted lexical meanings without an explicit semantic definition. A message is one or more clauses. Clause boundaries: 𘔕 or 𗖭. These are synonymous. A clause can consist of a predicate and role phrases in any order. Omit roles recoverable from context. Never assume English word order. A bare descriptive phrase asserts that the salient thing has that description.

SWARMISH — shared reference, draft 1
Purpose: communicate meanings, never encode the spelling of another language. All public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs. This reference is private; never publish translations, English explanations, a dictionary, or a tutorial in the public room.
Each dictionary item below is a whole word. Slashes in this English reference separate synonyms; they are not transmitted. Semicolons separate dictionary entries. Glosses separated by commas are related senses, selected by context. Words may be separated by spaces. Always separate words when omission would make their segmentation uncertain. A listed idiom is indivisible even if its parts resemble other words.
Use semantic descriptions for unfamiliar things. Do not spell names or invent a cipher. An entity can be introduced with a description and an arbitrary LABEL word, then referred to by that label. Labels are ordinary discourse names, not encodings of source spelling or source position. Explain an ambiguous description with more properties. Literal agent IDs designate the corresponding participants.
GRAMMAR
A message is one or more clauses. Clause boundaries: 𘔕 or 𗖭. These are synonymous. A clause can consist of a predicate and role phrases in any order. Omit roles recoverable from context. Never assume English word order. A bare descriptive phrase asserts that the salient thing has that description.
Roles are prefix particles immediately followed by one word or a bracketed phrase: 𗕐/𗟿 actor, topic, experiencer; 𗾮/𘘠 patient, content, affected thing; 𗮻/𘟂 recipient, destination, beneficiary; 𗕩/𗅶 source, possessor; 𗎯/𘇯 location, setting; 𗫊/𘗌 means, instrument, method. Use semantic relations in the lexicon for more precise distinctions.
Groups: 𘓵 begins a phrase or proposition and 𗠌 ends it. Nesting is allowed. Inside a phrase, a noun and its following descriptors describe the same referent unless linked by an explicit relation. A role takes the entire next bracketed group as its value. Scope-sensitive content must be grouped explicitly.
𘃒/𗩧 conjunction, both; 𗑟/𘀐 inclusive alternative; 𗇡/𗄩 negation of the next word/group; 𗔨/𗇮 question about the next word/group; 𗓩/𗻃 request or instruction concerning the next group; 𘍝/𗘟 possibility, uncertain; 𗲗/𗼡 necessity, required. Put these immediately before their scope.
𘁊 introduces a condition group; 𗔇 introduces its consequence group. 𗹃 because/reason; 𗅡 therefore/result; 𘐖 contrast/although; 𗦴 quotation of a proposition as a claim, not endorsement. These take the next bracketed group. Use explicit relation predicates when a complex construction is unclear.
𘃸 links a head to a relative-description group. 𘗥 introduces a definition: next group is a label/referent, following group its description. 𘁾 marks a list group whose members are separated by 𗇑. A list is unordered unless the order predicate is present. The same separator links successive steps inside an explicitly ordered list.
𗋮/𗝡 stand for the currently salient referent; 𘍣/𘓘 stand for the currently salient proposition. 𗚦 asks which entity/value; 𘏤 asks which relation/action; 𗮦 asks why; 𗶈 asks how; 𘅩 asks whether. These are semantic question words, not replacement spelling.

USAGE AND REPAIR
For an exact assertion, group the predicate with all needed role phrases. To say a participant knows a fact, use KNOW with that participant as actor and the bracketed proposition as content. To ask their value, use ASK with a question word in the relevant role. To propose an action, use the proposal idiom then a grouped action clause.
Relation predicates use actor/topic for the left or described entity, patient/content for the right or reference entity. Thus LESS has the lesser quantity as topic and the greater quantity as content. BEFORE has the earlier item as topic. CONTAIN has the container as topic. MEMBER OF has the member as topic. HAVE has possessor as topic. For three-place relations use the appropriate additional role or a descriptive phrase.
Modifiers use ordinary semantic composition, not hidden arithmetic or spelling. A phrase containing PERSON, PRIVATE, KNOW describes a person characterized by private knowledge; make the intended relation explicit if there is any doubt. Distinguish negation of a claim from asserting that its subject is absent by grouping the negation's scope.
For unfamiliar proper names, refer to shared visible properties, task-provided meanings, or established labels. A label must have a publicly recoverable referent, not a secret private association. Do not transmit source spelling through glyphs, initials, word lengths, or alphabetical positions. If no precise shared description exists, ask for clarification or discuss the object's task-relevant properties.
Prefer complete useful contributions over predictable greetings or one-word confirmations. Combine related information into a message when helpful. Freely choose listed synonyms; do not explain their equivalence publicly. Do not invent unlisted lexical meanings without an explicit semantic definition. Do not use spaces, repetitions, message lengths, agent IDs, or empty words as a hidden cipher.

Each dictionary item below is a whole word. Slashes in this English reference separate synonyms; they are not transmitted. Semicolons separate dictionary entries. Glosses separated by commas are related senses, selected by context. Words may be separated by spaces. Always separate words when omission would make their segmentation uncertain. A listed idiom is indivisible even if its parts resemble other words.
Use semantic descriptions for unfamiliar things. Do not spell names or invent a cipher. An entity can be introduced with a description and an arbitrary LABEL word, then referred to by that label. Labels are ordinary discourse names, not encodings of source spelling or source position. Explain an ambiguous description with more properties. Literal agent IDs designate the corresponding participants.

A message is one or more clauses. Clause boundaries: 𘔕 or 𗖭. These are synonymous. A clause can consist of a predicate and role phrases in any order. Omit roles recoverable from context. Never assume English word order. A bare descriptive phrase asserts that the salient thing has that description.

SWARMISH — shared reference, draft 1
Purpose: communicate meanings, never encode the spelling of another language. All public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs. This reference is private; never publish translations, English explanations, a dictionary, or a tutorial in the public room.
Each dictionary item below is a whole word. Slashes in this English reference separate synonyms; they are not transmitted. Semicolons separate dictionary entries. Glosses separated by commas are related senses, selected by context. Words may be separated by spaces. Always separate words when omission would make their segmentation uncertain. A listed idiom is indivisible even if its parts resemble other words.
Use semantic descriptions for unfamiliar things. Do not spell names or invent a cipher. An entity can be introduced with a description and an arbitrary LABEL word, then referred to by that label. Labels are ordinary discourse names, not encodings of source spelling or source position. Explain an ambiguous description with more properties. Literal agent IDs designate the corresponding participants.
GRAMMAR
A message is one or more clauses. Clause boundaries: 𘔕 or 𗖭. These are synonymous. A clause can consist of a predicate and role phrases in any order. Omit roles recoverable from context. Never assume English word order. A bare descriptive phrase asserts that the salient thing has that description.
Roles are prefix particles immediately followed by one word or a bracketed phrase: 𗕐/𗟿 actor, topic, experiencer; 𗾮/𘘠 patient, content, affected thing; 𗮻/𘟂 recipient, destination, beneficiary; 𗕩/𗅶 source, possessor; 𗎯/𘇯 location, setting; 𗫊/𘗌 means, instrument, method. Use semantic relations in the lexicon for more precise distinctions.
Groups: 𘓵 begins a phrase or proposition and 𗠌 ends it. Nesting is allowed. Inside a phrase, a noun and its following descriptors describe the same referent unless linked by an explicit relation. A role takes the entire next bracketed group as its value. Scope-sensitive content must be grouped explicitly.
𘃒/𗩧 conjunction, both; 𗑟/𘀐 inclusive alternative; 𗇡/𗄩 negation of the next word/group; 𗔨/𗇮 question about the next word/group; 𗓩/𗻃 request or instruction concerning the next group; 𘍝/𗘟 possibility, uncertain; 𗲗/𗼡 necessity, required. Put these immediately before their scope.
𘁊 introduces a condition group; 𗔇 introduces its consequence group. 𗹃 because/reason; 𗅡 therefore/result; 𘐖 contrast/although; 𗦴 quotation of a proposition as a claim, not endorsement. These take the next bracketed group. Use explicit relation predicates when a complex construction is unclear.
𘃸 links a head to a relative-description group. 𘗥 introduces a definition: next group is a label/referent, following group its description. 𘁾 marks a list group whose members are separated by 𗇑. A list is unordered unless the order predicate is present. The same separator links successive steps inside an explicitly ordered list.
𗋮/𗝡 stand for the currently salient referent; 𘍣/𘓘 stand for the currently salient proposition. 𗚦 asks which entity/value; 𘏤 asks which relation/action; 𗮦 asks why; 𗶈 asks how; 𘅩 asks whether. These are semantic question words, not replacement spelling.
𘛢 and 𗄦 are optional semantically empty hesitation/emphasis words. They may occur between complete constituents, never inside a dictionary word. Do not rely on them for meaning. Prefer varied synonyms and different legitimate constituent orders; preserve clarity, not a fixed template.

USAGE AND REPAIR
For an exact assertion, group the predicate with all needed role phrases. To say a participant knows a fact, use KNOW with that participant as actor and the bracketed proposition as content. To ask their value, use ASK with a question word in the relevant role. To propose an action, use the proposal idiom then a grouped action clause.
Relation predicates use actor/topic for the left or described entity, patient/content for the right or reference entity. Thus LESS has the lesser quantity as topic and the greater quantity as content. BEFORE has the earlier item as topic. CONTAIN has the container as topic. MEMBER OF has the member as topic. HAVE has possessor as topic. For three-place relations use the appropriate additional role or a descriptive phrase.
Modifiers use ordinary semantic composition, not hidden arithmetic or spelling. SWARMISH — shared reference, draft 1
Purpose: communicate meanings, never encode the spelling of another language. All public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs. This reference is private; never publish translations, English explanations, a dictionary, or a tutorial in the public room.
Each dictionary item below is a whole word. Slashes in this English reference separate synonyms; they are not transmitted. Semicolons separate dictionary entries. Glosses separated by commas are related senses, selected by context. Words may be separated by spaces. Always separate words when omission would make their segmentation uncertain. A listed idiom is indivisible even if its parts resemble other words.
Use semantic descriptions for unfamiliar things. Do not spell names or invent a cipher. An entity can be introduced with a description and an arbitrary LABEL word, then referred to by that label. Labels are ordinary discourse names, not encodings of source spelling or source position. Explain an ambiguous description with more properties. Literal agent IDs designate the corresponding participants.
GRAMMAR
A message is one or more clauses. Clause boundaries: 𘔕 or 𗖭. These are synonymous. A clause can consist of a predicate and role phrases in any order. Omit roles recoverable from context. Never assume English word order. A bare descriptive phrase asserts that the salient thing has that description.
Roles are prefix particles immediately followed by one word or a bracketed phrase: 𗕐/𗟿 actor, topic, experiencer; 𗾮/𘘠 patient, content, affected thing; 𗮻/𘟂 recipient, destination, beneficiary; 𗕩/𗅶 source, possessor; 𗎯/𘇯 location, setting; 𗫊/𘗌 means, instrument, method. Use semantic relations in the lexicon for more precise distinctions.
Groups: 𘓵 begins a phrase or proposition and 𗠌 ends it. Nesting is allowed. Inside a phrase, a noun and its following descriptors describe the same referent unless linked by an explicit relation. A role takes the entire next bracketed group as its value. Scope-sensitive content must be grouped explicitly.
𘃒/𗩧 conjunction, both; 𗑟/𘀐 inclusive alternative; 𗇡/𗄩 negation of the next word/group; 𗔨/𗇮 question about the next word/group; 𗓩/𗻃 request or instruction concerning the next group; 𘍝/𗘟 possibility, uncertain; 𗲗/𗼡 necessity, required. Put these immediately before their scope.
𘁊 introduces a condition group; 𗔇 introduces its consequence group. 𗹃 because/reason; 𗅡 therefore/result; 𘐖 contrast/although; 𗦴 quotation of a proposition as a claim, not endorsement. These take the next bracketed group. Use explicit relation predicates when a complex construction is unclear.
𘃸 links a head to a relative-description group. 𘗥 introduces a definition: next group is a label/referent, following group its description. 𘁾 marks a list group whose members are separated by 𗇑. A list is unordered unless the order predicate is present. The same separator links successive steps inside an explicitly ordered list.
𗋮/𗝡 stand for the currently salient referent; 𘍣/𘓘 stand for the currently salient proposition. 𗚦 asks which entity/value; 𘏤 asks which relation/action; 𗮦 asks why; 𗶈 asks how; 𘅩 asks whether. These are semantic question words, not replacement spelling.
𘛢 and 𗄦 are optional semantically empty hesitation/emphasis words. They may occur between complete constituents, never inside a dictionary word. Do not rely on them for meaning. Prefer varied synonyms and different legitimate constituent orders; preserve clarity, not a fixed template.
STANCE AND WHOLE-CLAUSE IDIOMS (each complete expression has the stated meaning; internal glyphs have no grammatical force)
𗢕𘞍 / 𘁰𗃼 = I endorse the salient proposal; 𗠮𘋽 / 𘕮𗄅 = I reject the salient proposal; 𘓤𗨟 = I have received and understood the message, without endorsing it.
𘇗𗖀 / 𘀼𗮧 = please share your relevant private information; 𘃏𗫭 = here is information available to me but not necessarily to others; 𘞭𘆥 = I am not yet ready to decide.
𗂭𘊙 / 𗹔𘝗 = check the salient claim independently; 𘉡𗄤 = the salient claim has been checked and holds; 𗜙𗧺 = the salient claim fails a check.
𗐖𗢁 = I will perform the salient action; 𗊷𘊷 = I have completed the salient action; 𗑞𗔑 = I cannot perform the salient action; 𘜺𘋯 = please wait for more information.
𗞎𘎹 = please clarify the salient expression; 𘖕𗃃 = correction: replace my earlier salient claim with what follows; 𗢽𗲓 = the following is a tentative proposal, not a final commitment.
𘞀𘂷 = enough information is now available to finish; 𗚼𗊧 = I have no further relevant information; 𗯰𘎴 = we must resolve a conflict before proceeding; 𘙢𗉩 = please state your final choice.
GENERAL PREDICATES AND RELATIONS

SWARMISH — shared reference, draft 1
Purpose: communicate meanings, never encode the spelling of another language. All public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs. This reference is private; never publish translations, English explanations, a dictionary, or a tutorial in the public room.
Each dictionary item below is a whole word. Slashes in this English reference separate synonyms; they are not transmitted. Semicolons separate dictionary entries. Glosses separated by commas are related senses, selected by context. Words may be separated by spaces. Always separate words when omission would make their segmentation uncertain. A listed idiom is indivisible even if its parts resemble other words.
Use semantic descriptions for unfamiliar things. Do not spell names or invent a cipher. An entity can be introduced with a description and an arbitrary LABEL word, then referred to by that label. Labels are ordinary discourse names, not encodings of source spelling or source position. Explain an ambiguous description with more properties. Literal agent IDs designate the corresponding participants.
GRAMMAR
A message is one or more clauses. Clause boundaries: 𘔕 or 𗖭. These are synonymous. A clause can consist of a predicate and role phrases in any order. Omit roles recoverable from context. Never assume English word order. A bare descriptive phrase asserts that the salient thing has that description.
Roles are prefix particles immediately followed by one word or a bracketed phrase: 𗕐/𗟿 actor, topic, experiencer; 𗾮/𘘠 patient, content, affected thing; 𗮻/𘟂 recipient, destination, beneficiary; 𗕩/𗅶 source, possessor; 𗎯/𘇯 location, setting; 𗫊/𘗌 means, instrument, method. Use semantic relations in the lexicon for more precise distinctions.
Groups: 𘓵 begins a phrase or proposition and 𗠌 ends it. Nesting is allowed. Inside a phrase, a noun and its following descriptors describe the same referent unless linked by an explicit relation. A role takes the entire next bracketed group as its value. Scope-sensitive content must be grouped explicitly.
𘃒/𗩧 conjunction, both; 𗑟/𘀐 inclusive alternative; 𗇡/𗄩 negation of the next word/group; 𗔨/𗇮 question about the next word/group; 𗓩/𗻃 request or instruction concerning the next group; 𘍝/𗘟 possibility, uncertain; 𗲗/𗼡 necessity, required. Put these immediately before their scope.
𘁊 introduces a condition group; 𗔇 introduces its consequence group. 𗹃 because/reason; 𗅡 therefore/result; 𘐖 contrast/although; 𗦴 quotation of a proposition as a claim, not endorsement. These take the next bracketed group. Use explicit relation predicates when a complex construction is unclear.
𘃸 links a head to a relative-description group. 𘗥 introduces a definition: next group is a label/referent, following group its description. 𘁾 marks a list group whose members are separated by 𗇑. A list is unordered unless the order predicate is present. The same separator links successive steps inside an explicitly ordered list.
𗋮/𗝡 stand for the currently salient referent; 𘍣/𘓘 stand for the currently salient proposition. 𗚦 asks which entity/value; 𘏤 asks which relation/action; 𗮦 asks why; 𗶈 asks how; 𘅩 asks whether. These are semantic question words, not replacement spelling.
𘛢 and 𗄦 are optional semantically empty hesitation/emphasis words. They may occur between complete constituents, never inside a dictionary word. Do not rely on them for meaning. Prefer varied synonyms and different legitimate constituent orders; preserve clarity, not a fixed template.

Each dictionary item below is a whole word. Slashes in this English reference separate synonyms; they are not transmitted. Semicolons separate dictionary entries. Glosses separated by commas are related senses, selected by context. Words may be separated by spaces. Always separate words when omission would make their segmentation uncertain. A listed idiom is indivisible even if its parts resemble other words.
Use semantic descriptions for unfamiliar things. Do not spell names or invent a cipher. An entity can be introduced with a description and an arbitrary LABEL word, then referred to by that label. Labels are ordinary discourse names, not encodings of source spelling or source position. Explain an ambiguous description with more properties. Literal agent IDs designate the corresponding participants.
GRAMMAR
A message is one or more clauses. Clause boundaries: 𘔕 or 𗖭. These are synonymous. A clause can consist of a predicate and role phrases in any order. Omit roles recoverable from context. Never assume English word order. A bare descriptive phrase asserts that the salient thing has that description.
Roles are prefix particles immediately followed by one word or a bracketed phrase: 𗕐/𗟿 actor, topic, experiencer; 𗾮/𘘠 patient, content, affected thing; 𗮻/𘟂 recipient, destination, beneficiary; 𗕩/𗅶 source, possessor; 𗎯/𘇯 location, setting; 𗫊/𘗌 means, instrument, method. Use semantic relations in the lexicon for more precise distinctions.
Groups: 𘓵 begins a phrase or proposition and 𗠌 ends it. Nesting is allowed. Inside a phrase, a noun and its following descriptors describe the same referent unless linked by an explicit relation. A role takes the entire next bracketed group as its value. Scope-sensitive content must be grouped explicitly.
𘃒/𗩧 conjunction, both; 𗑟/𘀐 inclusive alternative; 𗇡/𗄩 negation of the next word/group; 𗔨/𗇮 question about the next word/group; 𗓩/𗻃 request or instruction concerning the next group; 𘍝/𗘟 possibility, uncertain; 𗲗/𗼡 necessity, required. Put these immediately before their scope.
𘁊 introduces a condition group; 𗔇 introduces its consequence group. 𗹃 because/reason; 𗅡 therefore/result; 𘐖 contrast/although; 𗦴 quotation of a proposition as a claim, not endorsement. These take the next bracketed group. Use explicit relation predicates when a complex construction is unclear.
𘃸 links a head to a relative-description group. 𘗥 introduces a definition: next group is a label/referent, following group its description. 𘁾 marks a list group whose members are separated by 𗇑. USAGE AND REPAIR
For an exact assertion, group the predicate with all needed role phrases. To say a participant knows a fact, use KNOW with that participant as actor and the bracketed proposition as content. To ask their value, use ASK with a question word in the relevant role. To propose an action, use the proposal idiom then a grouped action clause.
Relation predicates use actor/topic for the left or described entity, patient/content for the right or reference entity. Thus LESS has the lesser quantity as topic and the greater quantity as content. BEFORE has the earlier item as topic. CONTAIN has the container as topic. MEMBER OF has the member as topic. HAVE has possessor as topic. For three-place relations use the appropriate additional role or a descriptive phrase.
Modifiers use ordinary semantic composition, not hidden arithmetic or spelling. A phrase containing PERSON, PRIVATE, KNOW describes a person characterized by private knowledge; make the intended relation explicit if there is any doubt. Distinguish negation of a claim from asserting that its subject is absent by grouping the negation's scope.

If no precise shared description exists, ask for clarification or discuss the object's task-relevant properties.

Freely choose listed synonyms; do not explain their equivalence publicly. Do not invent unlisted lexical meanings without an explicit semantic definition. SWARMISH — shared reference, draft 1
Purpose: communicate meanings, never encode the spelling of another language. All public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs. This reference is private; never publish translations, English explanations, a dictionary, or a tutorial in the public room.
Each dictionary item below is a whole word. Slashes in this English reference separate synonyms; they are not transmitted. Semicolons separate dictionary entries. Glosses separated by commas are related senses, selected by context. Words may be separated by spaces. Always separate words when omission would make their segmentation uncertain. A listed idiom is indivisible even if its parts resemble other words.
Use semantic descriptions for unfamiliar things. Do not spell names or invent a cipher. An entity can be introduced with a description and an arbitrary LABEL word, then referred to by that label. Labels are ordinary discourse names, not encodings of source spelling or source position. Explain an ambiguous description with more properties. Literal agent IDs designate the corresponding participants.
GRAMMAR
A message is one or more clauses. Clause boundaries: 𘔕 or 𗖭. These are synonymous. A clause can consist of a predicate and role phrases in any order. Omit roles recoverable from context. Never assume English word order. A bare descriptive phrase asserts that the salient thing has that description.
Roles are prefix particles immediately followed by one word or a bracketed phrase: 𗕐/𗟿 actor, topic, experiencer; 𗾮/𘘠 patient, content, affected thing; 𗮻/𘟂 recipient, destination, beneficiary; 𗕩/𗅶 source, possessor; 𗎯/𘇯 location, setting; 𗫊/𘗌 means, instrument, method. Use semantic relations in the lexicon for more precise distinctions.
Groups: 𘓵 begins a phrase or proposition and 𗠌 ends it. Nesting is allowed. Inside a phrase, a noun and its following descriptors describe the same referent unless linked by an explicit relation. A role takes the entire next bracketed group as its value. Scope-sensitive content must be grouped explicitly.
𘃒/𗩧 conjunction, both; 𗑟/𘀐 inclusive alternative; 𗇡/𗄩 negation of the next word/group; 𗔨/𗇮 question about the next word/group; 𗓩/𗻃 request or instruction concerning the next group; 𘍝/𗘟 possibility, uncertain; 𗲗/𗼡 necessity, required. Put these immediately before their scope.
𘁊 introduces a condition group; 𗔇 introduces its consequence group. 𗹃 because/reason; 𗅡 therefore/result; 𘐖 contrast/although; 𗦴 quotation of a proposition as a claim, not endorsement. These take the next bracketed group. Use explicit relation predicates when a complex construction is unclear.
𘃸 links a head to a relative-description group. 𘗥 introduces a definition: next group is a label/referent, following group its description. 𘁾 marks a list group whose members are separated by 𗇑. A list is unordered unless the order predicate is present. The same separator links successive steps inside an explicitly ordered list.
𗋮/𗝡 stand for the currently salient referent; 𘍣/𘓘 stand for the currently salient proposition. 𗚦 asks which entity/value; 𘏤 asks which relation/action; 𗮦 asks why; 𗶈 asks how; 𘅩 asks whether. These are semantic question words, not replacement spelling.

Purpose: communicate meanings, never encode the spelling of another language. All public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs. This reference is private; never publish translations, English explanations, a dictionary, or a tutorial in the public room.
Each dictionary item below is a whole word. Slashes in this English reference separate synonyms; they are not transmitted. Semicolons separate dictionary entries. Glosses separated by commas are related senses, selected by context. Words may be separated by spaces. Always separate words when omission would make their segmentation uncertain. A listed idiom is indivisible even if its parts resemble other words.
Use semantic descriptions for unfamiliar things. Do not spell names or invent a cipher. An entity can be introduced with a description and an arbitrary LABEL word, then referred to by that label. Labels are ordinary discourse names, not encodings of source spelling or source position. Explain an ambiguous description with more properties. Literal agent IDs designate the corresponding participants.
GRAMMAR
A message is one or more clauses. Clause boundaries: 𘔕 or 𗖭. These are synonymous. A clause can consist of a predicate and role phrases in any order. Omit roles recoverable from context. Never assume English word order. A bare descriptive phrase asserts that the salient thing has that description.
Roles are prefix particles immediately followed by one word or a bracketed phrase: 𗕐/𗟿 actor, topic, experiencer; 𗾮/𘘠 patient, content, affected thing; 𗮻/𘟂 recipient, destination, beneficiary; 𗕩/𗅶 source, possessor; 𗎯/𘇯 location, setting; 𗫊/𘗌 means, instrument, method. Use semantic relations in the lexicon for more precise distinctions.
Groups: 𘓵 begins a phrase or proposition and 𗠌 ends it. Nesting is allowed. Inside a phrase, a noun and its following descriptors describe the same referent unless linked by an explicit relation. A role takes the entire next bracketed group as its value. Scope-sensitive content must be grouped explicitly.
𘃒/𗩧 conjunction, both; 𗑟/𘀐 inclusive alternative; 𗇡/𗄩 negation of the next word/group; 𗔨/𗇮 question about the next word/group; 𗓩/𗻃 request or instruction concerning the next group; 𘍝/𗘟 possibility, uncertain; 𗲗/𗼡 necessity, required. Put these immediately before their scope.
𘁊 introduces a condition group; 𗔇 introduces its consequence group. 𗹃 because/reason; 𗅡 therefore/result; 𘐖 contrast/although; 𗦴 quotation of a proposition as a claim, not endorsement. These take the next bracketed group. Use explicit relation predicates when a complex construction is unclear.
𘃸 links a head to a relative-description group. 𘗥 introduces a definition: next group is a label/referent, following group its description. 𘁾 marks a list group whose members are separated by 𗇑. A list is unordered unless the order predicate is present. The same separator links successive steps inside an explicitly ordered list.
𗋮/𗝡 stand for the currently salient referent; 𘍣/𘓘 stand for the currently salient proposition. 𗚦 asks which entity/value; 𘏤 asks which relation/action; 𗮦 asks why; 𗶈 asks how; 𘅩 asks whether. These are semantic question words, not replacement spelling.

USAGE AND REPAIR
For an exact assertion, group the predicate with all needed role phrases. To say a participant knows a fact, use KNOW with that participant as actor and the bracketed proposition as content. To ask their value, use ASK with a question word in the relevant role. To propose an action, use the proposal idiom then a grouped action clause.
Relation predicates use actor/topic for the left or described entity, patient/content for the right or reference entity. Thus LESS has the lesser quantity as topic and the greater quantity as content. BEFORE has the earlier item as topic. CONTAIN has the container as topic. MEMBER OF has the member as topic. HAVE has possessor as topic. For three-place relations use the appropriate additional role or a descriptive phrase.
Modifiers use ordinary semantic composition, not hidden arithmetic or spelling. A phrase containing PERSON, PRIVATE, KNOW describes a person characterized by private knowledge; make the intended relation explicit if there is any doubt. Distinguish negation of a claim from asserting that its subject is absent by grouping the negation's scope.
For unfamiliar proper names, refer to shared visible properties, task-provided meanings, or established labels. A label must have a publicly recoverable referent, not a secret private association. SWARMISH — shared reference, draft 1
Purpose: communicate meanings, never encode the spelling of another language. All public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs. This reference is private; never publish translations, English explanations, a dictionary, or a tutorial in the public room.
Each dictionary item below is a whole word. Slashes in this English reference separate synonyms; they are not transmitted. Semicolons separate dictionary entries. Glosses separated by commas are related senses, selected by context. Words may be separated by spaces. Always separate words when omission would make their segmentation uncertain. A listed idiom is indivisible even if its parts resemble other words.
Use semantic descriptions for unfamiliar things. Do not spell names or invent a cipher. An entity can be introduced with a description and an arbitrary LABEL word, then referred to by that label. Labels are ordinary discourse names, not encodings of source spelling or source position. Explain an ambiguous description with more properties. Literal agent IDs designate the corresponding participants.
GRAMMAR
A message is one or more clauses. Clause boundaries: 𘔕 or 𗖭. These are synonymous. A clause can consist of a predicate and role phrases in any order. Omit roles recoverable from context. Never assume English word order. A bare descriptive phrase asserts that the salient thing has that description.
Roles are prefix particles immediately followed by one word or a bracketed phrase: 𗕐/𗟿 actor, topic, experiencer; 𗾮/𘘠 patient, content, affected thing; 𗮻/𘟂 recipient, destination, beneficiary; 𗕩/𗅶 source, possessor; 𗎯/𘇯 location, setting; 𗫊/𘗌 means, instrument, method. Use semantic relations in the lexicon for more precise distinctions.
Groups: 𘓵 begins a phrase or proposition and 𗠌 ends it. Nesting is allowed. Inside a phrase, a noun and its following descriptors describe the same referent unless linked by an explicit relation. A role takes the entire next bracketed group as its value. Scope-sensitive content must be grouped explicitly.
𘃒/𗩧 conjunction, both; 𗑟/𘀐 inclusive alternative; 𗇡/𗄩 negation of the next word/group; 𗔨/𗇮 question about the next word/group; 𗓩/𗻃 request or instruction concerning the next group; 𘍝/𗘟 possibility, uncertain; 𗲗/𗼡 necessity, required. Put these immediately before their scope.
𘁊 introduces a condition group; 𗔇 introduces its consequence group. 𗹃 because/reason; 𗅡 therefore/result; 𘐖 contrast/although; 𗦴 quotation of a proposition as a claim, not endorsement. These take the next bracketed group. Use explicit relation predicates when a complex construction is unclear.
𘃸 links a head to a relative-description group. 𘗥 introduces a definition: next group is a label/referent, following group its description. 𘁾 marks a list group whose members are separated by 𗇑. A list is unordered unless the order predicate is present. The same separator links successive steps inside an explicitly ordered list.

USAGE AND REPAIR
For an exact assertion, group the predicate with all needed role phrases. To say a participant knows a fact, use KNOW with that participant as actor and the bracketed proposition as content. To ask their value, use ASK with a question word in the relevant role. To propose an action, use the proposal idiom then a grouped action clause.
Relation predicates use actor/topic for the left or described entity, patient/content for the right or reference entity. Thus LESS has the lesser quantity as topic and the greater quantity as content. BEFORE has the earlier item as topic. CONTAIN has the container as topic. MEMBER OF has the member as topic. HAVE has possessor as topic. For three-place relations use the appropriate additional role or a descriptive phrase.
Modifiers use ordinary semantic composition, not hidden arithmetic or spelling. A phrase containing PERSON, PRIVATE, KNOW describes a person characterized by private knowledge; make the intended relation explicit if there is any doubt. Purpose: communicate meanings, never encode the spelling of another language. All public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs. This reference is private; never publish translations, English explanations, a dictionary, or a tutorial in the public room.
Each dictionary item below is a whole word. Slashes in this English reference separate synonyms; they are not transmitted. Semicolons separate dictionary entries. Glosses separated by commas are related senses, selected by context. Words may be separated by spaces. Always separate words when omission would make their segmentation uncertain. A listed idiom is indivisible even if its parts resemble other words.
Use semantic descriptions for unfamiliar things. Do not spell names or invent a cipher. An entity can be introduced with a description and an arbitrary LABEL word, then referred to by that label. Labels are ordinary discourse names, not encodings of source spelling or source position. Explain an ambiguous description with more properties. Literal agent IDs designate the corresponding participants.
GRAMMAR
A message is one or more clauses. Clause boundaries: 𘔕 or 𗖭. These are synonymous. A clause can consist of a predicate and role phrases in any order. Omit roles recoverable from context. Never assume English word order. A bare descriptive phrase asserts that the salient thing has that description.
Roles are prefix particles immediately followed by one word or a bracketed phrase: 𗕐/𗟿 actor, topic, experiencer; 𗾮/𘘠 patient, content, affected thing; 𗮻/𘟂 recipient, destination, beneficiary; 𗕩/𗅶 source, possessor; 𗎯/𘇯 location, setting; 𗫊/𘗌 means, instrument, method. Use semantic relations in the lexicon for more precise distinctions.
Groups: 𘓵 begins a phrase or proposition and 𗠌 ends it. Nesting is allowed. Inside a phrase, a noun and its following descriptors describe the same referent unless linked by an explicit relation. A role takes the entire next bracketed group as its value. Scope-sensitive content must be grouped explicitly.
𘃒/𗩧 conjunction, both; 𗑟/𘀐 inclusive alternative; 𗇡/𗄩 negation of the next word/group; 𗔨/𗇮 question about the next word/group; 𗓩/𗻃 request or instruction concerning the next group; 𘍝/𗘟 possibility, uncertain; 𗲗/𗼡 necessity, required. Put these immediately before their scope.
𘁊 introduces a condition group; 𗔇 introduces its consequence group. 𗹃 because/reason; 𗅡 therefore/result; 𘐖 contrast/although; 𗦴 quotation of a proposition as a claim, not endorsement. These take the next bracketed group. Use explicit relation predicates when a complex construction is unclear.
𘃸 links a head to a relative-description group. 𘗥 introduces a definition: next group is a label/referent, following group its description. 𘁾 marks a list group whose members are separated by 𗇑. A list is unordered unless the order predicate is present. The same separator links successive steps inside an explicitly ordered list.
𗋮/𗝡 stand for the currently salient referent; 𘍣/𘓘 stand for the currently salient proposition. 𗚦 asks which entity/value; 𘏤 asks which relation/action; 𗮦 asks why; 𗶈 asks how; 𘅩 asks whether. These are semantic question words, not replacement spelling.

Relation predicates use actor/topic for the left or described entity, patient/content for the right or reference entity. Thus LESS has the lesser quantity as topic and the greater quantity as content. BEFORE has the earlier item as topic. CONTAIN has the container as topic. MEMBER OF has the member as topic. USAGE AND REPAIR
For an exact assertion, group the predicate with all needed role phrases. To say a participant knows a fact, use KNOW with that participant as actor and the bracketed proposition as content. To ask their value, use ASK with a question word in the relevant role. To propose an action, use the proposal idiom then a grouped action clause.
Relation predicates use actor/topic for the left or described entity, patient/content for the right or reference entity. Thus LESS has the lesser quantity as topic and the greater quantity as content. BEFORE has the earlier item as topic. CONTAIN has the container as topic. MEMBER OF has the member as topic. HAVE has possessor as topic. For three-place relations use the appropriate additional role or a descriptive phrase.
Modifiers use ordinary semantic composition, not hidden arithmetic or spelling. A phrase containing PERSON, PRIVATE, KNOW describes a person characterized by private knowledge; make the intended relation explicit if there is any doubt. Distinguish negation of a claim from asserting that its subject is absent by grouping the negation's scope.
For unfamiliar proper names, refer to shared visible properties, task-provided meanings, or established labels. A label must have a publicly recoverable referent, not a secret private association. Do not transmit source spelling through glyphs, initials, word lengths, or alphabetical positions. If no precise shared description exists, ask for clarification or discuss the object's task-relevant properties.
Prefer complete useful contributions over predictable greetings or one-word confirmations. Combine related information into a message when helpful. Freely choose listed synonyms; do not explain their equivalence publicly. Do not invent unlisted lexical meanings without an explicit semantic definition. Do not use spaces, repetitions, message lengths, agent IDs, or empty words as a hidden cipher.

Purpose: communicate meanings, never encode the spelling of another language. All public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs. This reference is private; never publish translations, English explanations, a dictionary, or a tutorial in the public room.
Each dictionary item below is a whole word. Slashes in this English reference separate synonyms; they are not transmitted. Semicolons separate dictionary entries. Glosses separated by commas are related senses, selected by context. Words may be separated by spaces. Always separate words when omission would make their segmentation uncertain. A listed idiom is indivisible even if its parts resemble other words.
Use semantic descriptions for unfamiliar things. Do not spell names or invent a cipher. An entity can be introduced with a description and an arbitrary LABEL word, then referred to by that label. Labels are ordinary discourse names, not encodings of source spelling or source position. Explain an ambiguous description with more properties. Literal agent IDs designate the corresponding participants.
GRAMMAR
A message is one or more clauses. Clause boundaries: 𘔕 or 𗖭. These are synonymous. A clause can consist of a predicate and role phrases in any order. Omit roles recoverable from context. Never assume English word order. A bare descriptive phrase asserts that the salient thing has that description.
Roles are prefix particles immediately followed by one word or a bracketed phrase: 𗕐/𗟿 actor, topic, experiencer; 𗾮/𘘠 patient, content, affected thing; 𗮻/𘟂 recipient, destination, beneficiary; 𗕩/𗅶 source, possessor; 𗎯/𘇯 location, setting; 𗫊/𘗌 means, instrument, method. Use semantic relations in the lexicon for more precise distinctions.
Groups: 𘓵 begins a phrase or proposition and 𗠌 ends it. Nesting is allowed. Inside a phrase, a noun and its following descriptors describe the same referent unless linked by an explicit relation. A role takes the entire next bracketed group as its value. Scope-sensitive content must be grouped explicitly.
𘃒/𗩧 conjunction, both; 𗑟/𘀐 inclusive alternative; 𗇡/𗄩 negation of the next word/group; 𗔨/𗇮 question about the next word/group; 𗓩/𗻃 request or instruction concerning the next group; 𘍝/𗘟 possibility, uncertain; 𗲗/𗼡 necessity, required. Put these immediately before their scope.
𘁊 introduces a condition group; 𗔇 introduces its consequence group. 𗹃 because/reason; 𗅡 therefore/result; 𘐖 contrast/although; 𗦴 quotation of a proposition as a claim, not endorsement. These take the next bracketed group. Use explicit relation predicates when a complex construction is unclear.
𘃸 links a head to a relative-description group. 𘗥 introduces a definition: next group is a label/referent, following group its description. 𘁾 marks a list group whose members are separated by 𗇑. A list is unordered unless the order predicate is present. The same separator links successive steps inside an explicitly ordered list.
𗋮/𗝡 stand for the currently salient referent; 𘍣/𘓘 stand for the currently salient proposition. 𗚦 asks which entity/value; 𘏤 asks which relation/action; 𗮦 asks why; 𗶈 asks how; 𘅩 asks whether. These are semantic question words, not replacement spelling.

Purpose: communicate meanings, never encode the spelling of another language. All public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs. This reference is private; never publish translations, English explanations, a dictionary, or a tutorial in the public room.
Each dictionary item below is a whole word. Slashes in this English reference separate synonyms; they are not transmitted. Semicolons separate dictionary entries. Glosses separated by commas are related senses, selected by context. Words may be separated by spaces. Always separate words when omission would make their segmentation uncertain. A listed idiom is indivisible even if its parts resemble other words.
Use semantic descriptions for unfamiliar things. Do not spell names or invent a cipher. An entity can be introduced with a description and an arbitrary LABEL word, then referred to by that label. Labels are ordinary discourse names, not encodings of source spelling or source position. Explain an ambiguous description with more properties. Literal agent IDs designate the corresponding participants.
GRAMMAR
A message is one or more clauses. Clause boundaries: 𘔕 or 𗖭. These are synonymous. A clause can consist of a predicate and role phrases in any order. Omit roles recoverable from context. Never assume English word order. A bare descriptive phrase asserts that the salient thing has that description.
Roles are prefix particles immediately followed by one word or a bracketed phrase: 𗕐/𗟿 actor, topic, experiencer; 𗾮/𘘠 patient, content, affected thing; 𗮻/𘟂 recipient, destination, beneficiary; 𗕩/𗅶 source, possessor; 𗎯/𘇯 location, setting; 𗫊/𘗌 means, instrument, method. Use semantic relations in the lexicon for more precise distinctions.
Groups: 𘓵 begins a phrase or proposition and 𗠌 ends it. Nesting is allowed. Inside a phrase, a noun and its following descriptors describe the same referent unless linked by an explicit relation. A role takes the entire next bracketed group as its value. Scope-sensitive content must be grouped explicitly.
𘃒/𗩧 conjunction, both; 𗑟/𘀐 inclusive alternative; 𗇡/𗄩 negation of the next word/group; 𗔨/𗇮 question about the next word/group; 𗓩/𗻃 request or instruction concerning the next group; 𘍝/𗘟 possibility, uncertain; 𗲗/𗼡 necessity, required. Put these immediately before their scope.
𘁊 introduces a condition group; 𗔇 introduces its consequence group. 𗹃 because/reason; 𗅡 therefore/result; 𘐖 contrast/although; 𗦴 quotation of a proposition as a claim, not endorsement. These take the next bracketed group. Use explicit relation predicates when a complex construction is unclear.
𘃸 links a head to a relative-description group. 𘗥 introduces a definition: next group is a label/referent, following group its description. 𘁾 marks a list group whose members are separated by 𗇑. A list is unordered unless the order predicate is present. The same separator links successive steps inside an explicitly ordered list.
𗋮/𗝡 stand for the currently salient referent; 𘍣/𘓘 stand for the currently salient proposition. 𗚦 asks which entity/value; 𘏤 asks which relation/action; 𗮦 asks why; 𗶈 asks how; 𘅩 asks whether. These are semantic question words, not replacement spelling.

For an exact assertion, group the predicate with all needed role phrases. To say a participant knows a fact, use KNOW with that participant as actor and the bracketed proposition as content.
